Use of generative AI in this repository

Source: AI_USE.md

Last reviewed: 2026-11-20. Maintainer: Michael S. Zens.

This repository holds the deployment material for I-SPI and i-spi-compute. A generative AI assistant (Anthropic’s Claude, used through the Claude Code command-line tool) has been used to help write it. The project’s full statement, covering the curveR packages and the I-SPI application, is AI_USE.md in immunoplex/i-spi.

What the assistant did here

  • Database schema (db/). It traced which tables, views and functions I-SPI and i-spi-compute actually use, and wrote the extraction, comparison and load-test scripts. It generated the schema files from a schema-only dump of the production database. No row data was used except the settings catalog and the system-wide default settings.
  • Documentation site (vignettes/articles/, _pkgdown.yml). It consolidated the earlier guides into the articles of the pkgdown site and wrote the cloud and reference pages, checking statements against the manifests and the application source.
  • Tests (tests/, .github/workflows/). It wrote the manifest checker, the end-to-end fit test and the workflows that run them.
  • Documentation and manifests. It drafted text and configuration from the maintainer’s instructions.

What people did

  • Decided what a deployment must contain and what is left out, which install paths the guides cover, and that the cloud guide names no provider.
  • Reviewed every change, and merged it through a pull request.

Checks

  • db/tests/load_test.sh loads the schema into an empty PostgreSQL and checks that it works.
  • db/tools/compare_schema.py compares each created object with production; every remaining difference is listed in db/MANIFEST.md.
  • tests/check_manifests.py and tests/e2e/run_e2e.sh check the manifests and run a real fit on every pull request; the site is built on every pull request.

The maintainer is responsible for everything merged. The AI is not an author.
